description: Gmail connection is started, confirmed and disconnected by the business owner only, and a Gmail OAuth callback links nothing until the user who started it confirms it (COST-LEDGER-001 section 7 items 4 and 5; R0-07 review ST-2 and ST-3). GET /commerce/businesses/:b/gmail/auth-url, the new POST /commerce/businesses/:b/gmail/confirm and DELETE /commerce/businesses/:b/gmail carry AuthGuard + BusinessGuard and GmailService.assertConnectAuthority: the OWNER membership or Business.ownerId (the rule IdentityService.assertBusinessOwner applies) and SUPER_ADMIN (the BusinessGuard platform bypass); every other member gets 403 {code:'GMAIL_OWNER_ONLY'}. The signed OAuth state (HMAC-SHA256 with GOOGLE_STATE_SECRET, single use per process as R0-07 made it) now carries the initiating user id, the business id, a nonce and a 10-minute expiry. GET /commerce/gmail/callback stays public (Google redirects the browser; the web proxy forwards no session) and links nothing: a verified state that names a user has its code exchanged and the tokens stored as a PENDING connector_accounts row (provider GOOGLE, service GMAIL, tokens encrypted with encryptToken, settings {purpose, userId, nonce, pendingExpiresAt} with a 15-minute window; existing table, no schema change), then redirects gmail=pending&pending=<id>. Only that user, still the owner (or SUPER_ADMIN), confirming that id on that business within the window, once, activates it (Business.gmail*); anything else answers 404 {code:'GMAIL_PENDING_NOT_FOUND'} and links nothing. An expired, replayed, forged or user-less state redirects gmail=error&reason=invalid_state with no token exchange. Google's token exchange and userinfo are stubbed in process (no network). Run from apps/server against this packet's isolated, migrated database: npx vitest run test/gmail-connect-binding.integration.test.ts src/modules/commerce/gmail.service.spec.ts --reporter=json --outputFile=.proof/r0-cmf5-vitest.json, then node ../../scripts/proof-admission/evaluate.mjs --manifest ../../scripts/proof-admission/manifests/gmail-connect-binding.json --report .proof/r0-cmf5-vitest.json. Every passing case of the two files is required; allowAdditionalCases is true only because the integration suite carries two it.todo cases outside this write set (the web confirmation step; the google-suite connect and connector disconnect routes), which the evaluator would otherwise reject as unexpected; requireReportSuccess keeps every reported case binding. RED-BEFORE on pkt/R0-CMF4-SEND-EMAIL-ORDER-repair (acfda3e6; tests-first commit c788e635): the integration suite failed 19 of 25 (STAFF auth-url 200 with a Google URL; ADMIN and STAFF revenue:admin 200; the state named no user; the distinguished owner 403 from ModuleScopeGuard; the owner's state completed in a stranger's request redirected gmail=success and linked the stranger's mailbox; a signed user-less state linked; no confirm route; STAFF revenue:write DELETE gmail 200 and cleared the mailbox; B05 and B12 failed there only because their first step expects gmail=pending) and the spec failed 9 of 9. Passing on the base (negative controls): X01, A06 (non-member 403, anonymous 401), B06 (expired state), B07 (forged or edited state), C02 (owner disconnect), X02 (no outbound beyond the Google stub).
notes: Owner ruling D-11 (2026-10-31): business configuration is OWNER only. The mailbox invoices, reminders, receipts and quotes are sent from (GmailService.sendEmail) is business configuration, so connecting, replacing and disconnecting it follows D-11, as R0-08c did for plan changes. The rule is restated in GmailService.assertConnectAuthority (CommerceModule does not import IdentityModule), with the same two owner arms and the SUPER_ADMIN bypass. ModuleScopeGuard was removed from auth-url and DELETE gmail: a revenue scope admits no one the owner rule refuses, and ModuleScopeGuard refused a distinguished owner with no membership row. GET .../gmail/status and the inbox and send routes keep their revenue scopes.

PENDING storage: connector_accounts (ConnectorAccount) is an existing tenant-scoped table with no other reader or writer in apps/server; its token columns are ciphertext by contract (token-encryption-coverage HANDLED_ELSEWHERE), so the pending tokens go through core/crypto/token-crypto encryptToken and are decrypted only at confirmation, when they move to the Business.gmail* columns the Prisma token-encryption extension encrypts. Every call names businessId. A newer consent by the same user replaces that user's unconfirmed pending row, and pending rows of the business past the window are removed when a new one is staged. The pending id is gmc_ plus 24 random bytes (base64url) and reaches only the browser that completed consent.

The callback cannot be bound to a session on this base: the API authenticates by Bearer token only and the web proxy (apps/web/src/app/api/commerce/gmail/callback/route.ts) fetches the API server-to-server with no session, so binding is by the state's userId plus the authenticated confirmation. A foreign user's confirmation is refused at confirm time (403 GMAIL_OWNER_ONLY for a non-owner, 404 GMAIL_PENDING_NOT_FOUND for an owner or SUPER_ADMIN who is not the user the state names); the callback itself redirects gmail=error for expired, replayed, forged and user-less states.

Open, outside the write set (it.todo in the integration suite): (1) the web app does not yet confirm a pending connection: /app/commerce receives gmail=pending&pending=<id> and has no step that POSTs it to .../gmail/confirm, so until a web packet lands an owner's connection stays pending and expires; (2) POST /connect/google-suite/businesses/:b/auth-url with services [gmail] (core/connectors/google-suite.*, AuthGuard + BusinessGuard only, a state naming no user) still lets any member write Business.gmail*, and core/connectors/connector.controller.ts disconnect clears it; both need the same owner rule and binding.
